content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Orlando

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and documented project-management experience. Review PMI's specific hour requirements for your background—typically a bachelor's degree plus several years leading projects, or equivalent experience without a degree. Gather your project documentation before applying.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. Attend instructor-led sessions on your schedule, engage in real-time Q&A, and access course materials designed to build exam readiness. This formal education fulfills PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Create your PMI account, document your eligibility, and submit your formal application through PMI's system. Pay the exam fee once PMI approves your credentials. Granite PM Academy supports you through this process to ensure accurate, complete submission.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and instructor mentoring—to reinforce your bootcamp learning. Schedule your exam through PMI's testing partner. Take the computer-based test at an authorized testing center on your preferred date.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After earning your PMP, commit to a three-year renewal cycle. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through continuing education, project work, and professional activities. Renew your credential before expiration to keep your competitive advantage in your local job market.
